svg.title: B01 / CALDERA SENTINEL — Yellowstone Hydrothermal Observatory engineering mission profile
svg.desc: B01, CALDERA SENTINEL — Yellowstone Hydrothermal Observatory. Original project: Can Changes in Hot Spring Composition Reflect Decadal-Scale Deformation of the Yellowstone Caldera?. Session B: Earth & Environmental Engineering. Scientific question: Do changes in conservative-solute ratios improve prediction of independently measured caldera deformation on annual to decadal timescales? Testable hypothesis: After hydrologic adjustment, a subset of stable thermal features may show reproducible lagged chemistry–deformation associations; a null incremental forecast skill is an equally valuable result.. svg.text: Can Changes in Hot Spring Composition Reflect Decadal-Scale Deformation of the Yellowstone Caldera?
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Build a coupled hydrothermal and geodetic inference system that tests
whether spring chemistry contains information about deformation beyond
seasonality, recharge and sampling artifacts. The proposed contribution is
an honest forecast comparison with calibrated uncertainty, plus a physical
explanation of mixing; correlated records alone will not establish a
Do changes in conservative-solute ratios improve prediction of independently
measured caldera deformation on annual to decadal timescales?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
After hydrologic adjustment, a subset of stable thermal features may show
reproducible lagged chemistry–deformation associations; a null incremental
forecast skill is an equally valuable result.
Endmember chemistry may drift and must be estimated rather than fixed across
Different spring names and coordinates require a documented identity
Sparse annual water sampling cannot resolve fast events or prove causality.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Geodetic and hydrothermal footprints differ; chemistry changes can arise
from boiling, precipitation, recharge or sampling. Even useful prediction
